review_notes: I read all 384 lines. Most declarations are `theorem`s whose proofs build instances with `let` and use targeted `simp only`/`rw`, so they add nothing to the simp set. The one piece of reusable API is the equivalence `polynomialQuotientBaseChange` (lines 266–282) and its evaluation lemma `polynomialQuotientBaseChange_tmul` (lines 315–319). I compared them with the Mathlib simp lemmas the definition is built from: `Algebra.TensorProduct.tensorQuotientEquiv_apply_tmul` and `_symm_apply_tmul`, `MvPolynomial.algebraTensorAlgEquiv_tmul` and `Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq_mk`, all `@[simp]`. A grep shows that `polynomialQuotientBaseChange` is only used inside this file, at lines 312, 364 and 370–371. So the effect on other files is limited, but the interface would still be better if fixed now. Other places that use `simp` (line 175, `hyperplane_injective_descent`, the proof of the `_tmul` lemma) use it for normal targeted rewriting. I saw no wrong-way rewrites, competing rules or credible loops there. I couldn't run Lean, so I haven't checked that the proposed generalized lemma or the shorter `simp` proof compiles. The right-hand side might need `algebraMap K _ a * mk _ (map p)` instead of `a • ...`, depending on how `simp` normalizes the target.

polynomialQuotientBaseChange (K := K) I ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[R] Ideal.Quotient.mk I p) =

findings.problem: The only evaluation lemma for the new equivalence `polynomialQuotientBaseChange` has no `@[simp]` attribute and only covers the special input `1 ⊗ₜ mk I p`. There is also no lemma for the inverse direction. The definition is built in tactic mode (`refine ... ?_; change ...; rw ...`), so unfolding it is a poor way to compute with it. As a result, `simp` cannot reduce a term `polynomialQuotientBaseChange I (a ⊗ₜ mk I p)` to its natural normal form `a • mk _ (map (algebraMap R K) p)`. The one real use (lines 368–375) shows the cost: it needs two `change` steps that spell out the composite equivalence by hand, then a manual `rw` chain. Mathlib's pieces that make up this equivalence are all simp-normalised for a general `a ⊗ₜ t`, so this wrapper falls short of the API it is built from.
findings.proposed_change:
Generalize and tag the lemma, following `MvPolynomial.algebraTensorAlgEquiv_tmul`:
```lean
@[simp] lemma polynomialQuotientBaseChange_tmul (I : Ideal (MvPolynomial n R)) (a : K) (p : MvPolynomial n R) :
    polynomialQuotientBaseChange (K := K) I (a ⊗ₜ[R] Ideal.Quotient.mk I p) =
      a • Ideal.Quotient.mk _ (MvPolynomial.map (algebraMap R K) p)
```
Keep the current statement as a special case (`one_smul`). Optionally add the inverse lemma `polynomialQuotientBaseChange_symm_mk_map : (polynomialQuotientBaseChange I).symm (mk _ (map (algebraMap R K) p)) = 1 ⊗ₜ mk I p`, which matches `algebraTensorAlgEquiv_symm_map`. Then the end of `countable_model_with_elements` (the two `change` steps and the `rw` chain) could become something like `simp [e₀, hp₀, hp]`, relying on the simp lemma `Ideal.quotientEquivAlgOfEq_mk`. I have not checked this.
findings.benefit: Users of the equivalence get a canonical simp normal form for every pure tensor, not just `1 ⊗ₜ _`. This matches the surrounding Mathlib API, and fragile `change` steps that restate the composite definition are no longer needed. The inverse lemma lets `simp` also move from the polynomial-quotient side back to the tensor side.
